subject: Capacity routecard & pricing posture for reserved GPUs
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Miller <alex.miller@cloudten.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity routecard & pricing posture for reserved GPUs

Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and three asks so we can put together a concrete reserved-capacity quote and pilot plan. Attaching the traffic profile you promised and a rough capacity-options workbook for your reference.

What we captured on the call
- Target launch window: mid-June internal beta, public launch late Q3.
- Initial throughput target: ~12 qps (requests per second) peak for real-time chat (avg payload ~350 tokens req/resp).
- Monthly token baseline: 30M tokens/month, ramp to ~90M over 6 months as usage grows.
- Quality: planning to use an LLM comparable to a 13B dense model; willing to consider 8-bit quantization if latency/throughput tradeoffs are favorable.
- Security: must run in a dedicated VPC with customer-managed keys (discussed under Private; for Dedicated we can do VPC peering).

Open questions / asks (please confirm on reply)
1) Budget posture: what is your target $/1M tokens or monthly budget band for Dedicated capacity? (ballpark helps — e.g., $Xk–$Yk per 1M tokens or $monthly commit).
2) GPU preference: do you have a hard requirement for H100, or would an A100 80GB band be acceptable if the unit economics are ~20–35% lower?
3) Throughput floor: can you confirm SLOs for p50/p95 latency (target p95 < 250ms for single-turn chat or is multi-turn acceptable up to 500ms)?

Next steps from our side once you confirm the three asks:
- I’ll send an options sheet (reserved lanes by GPU band: A100/H100) showing per-1M token unit economics across token density scenarios and suggested commit tiers.
- Marissa will run a quick benchmark on the sample payload (if you can drop the sample traffic CSV in the Drive link attached).
- We can scope a 30-day pilot (reserved small lane + fallback to hosted) to validate latency and token economics before a larger commit.

Attachments: CloudTen_traffic_profile.csv (you mentioned), redwood_capacity_options_v2.xlsx

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Alex Miller <alex.miller@cloudten.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <p.desai@cloudten.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity routecard & pricing posture for reserved GPUs

Karthik — thanks for the recap and for the workbook. Quick answers inline below.

Budget posture: We don’t have an exact $/1M target yet; the procurement team gave a very wide band of $12k–$35k per 1M tokens depending on latency and SLA. If we can show <300ms p95 and consistent throughput, they’ll tolerate the higher end. If latency is closer to 500ms, budget will skew to the low end.

GPU preference: No hard requirement for H100; preference for H100 only if the delta on latency/throughput justifies ~30%+ premium. Otherwise A100 80GB would be our choice for price-performance.

Throughput / SLOs: For launch we need p50 ~80ms, p95 < 300ms for single-turn chat (responses up to 400 tokens). Multi-turn sessions can be allowed up to 500ms p95. Peak qps: 15 qps burstable to 25 for short periods.

Other notes:
- Token profile: attached CSV includes mix (avg ~350 tokens per end-to-end response).
- Procurement timeline: aim to have a vendor selected and contract signed by 30 June.

We’re open to a 30-day pilot that looks like: a small reserved lane (1–2 GPUs equivalent) + automatic fallback to hosted instances when utilization spikes. Please include pilot pricing and an SLA we can evaluate.

Appreciate you looping Marissa for the bench.

—Alex
Director of Platform | CloudTen
alex.miller@cloudten.com | +1 (212) 555-6022
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Miller <alex.miller@cloudten.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity routecard & pricing posture for reserved GPUs

Alex — appreciate the clarity on SLOs and budget band. I ran a quick pass on the traffic sample and sketched three pragmatic options for Dedicated reserved lanes. Attached is a simplified options sheet (excerpted here).

Option A — Cost‑conscious (A100 80GB band)- Reserved: 2x A100 80GB equivalent (continuous)- Expected steady throughput: ~12 qps (with short burst headroom to 25 qps using autoscale)- Token econ (est): $11k per 1M tokens at baseline 30M/mo, improves to ~$8.5k per 1M at 90M/mo commit (because of batching / KV cache benefits)- Latency: estimated p95 ~260–320ms depending on prompt length and KV cache hit rate

Option B — Balanced (mixed A100/H100 pool)- Reserved: 1x H100 + 1x A100 (balanced routing, model variant on H100 for low-latency flows)- Throughput: baseline 18 qps, burstable to 30 qps- Token econ (est): $16k per 1M tokens at 30M/mo, $12k at 90M/mo- Latency: estimated p95 ~180–240ms on H100 routed flows

Option C — Performance-first (H100 band)- Reserved: 2x H100 equivalent- Throughput: baseline 25 qps, strong headroom for token-dense responses- Token econ (est): $24k per 1M tokens at 30M/mo, $18k at 90M/mo- Latency: p95 ~120–180ms

Pilot proposal- 30-day pilot on Option A with an experiment add-on: route 30% of production traffic to a small H100 test lane during peak windows for 10 days to validate latency gains.- Pilot pricing: flat monthly pilot fee covering reserved lane + metered overage (we’ll present numbers in formal quote).

Next asks for CloudTen to finalize the quote
1) Confirm preferred option (A/B/C) or ask us to present a blended custom option.
2) Confirm whether the procurement team wants unit econ quoted as $/1M tokens or as committed monthly spend; they asked for both last time.
3) Confirm whether you want us to include a stronger SLA (e.g., 99.95% uptime, with credits) during pilot or reserve that for the full contract.

I’ll turn this into a quote draft if you confirm Option preference and procurement format.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_options_v2.xlsx, pilot-sow-draft.pdf

Thanks — Marissa
Sr. Customer Success & Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-3310
From: Alex Miller <alex.miller@cloudten.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity routecard & pricing posture for reserved GPUs

Marissa / Karthik — thanks, that breakdown is exactly what procurement asked for. We want to move forward with a 30-day pilot on Option A with the 10-day H100 spike test. Procurement prefers both quote formats ($/1M tokens and committed monthly spend) — please surface both in the draft.

A couple small asks for the pilot quote:
- Include explicit overage pricing if we exceed reserved lane (per-hour equivalent + per-token metric).
- Show staged discounts if we move to 90M/mo in months 4–6.
- We want the pilot to include logs and trace export to our SIEM (we’ll provide an onboarding ticket).

If you can get a formal pilot quote and SOW to us by next Tue (13 Apr), we’ll circulate to procurement and legal for a June 30 target sign date.

—Alex
